title: Kadison's similarity theorem through uniform derivation estimates
main_claim: Every bounded unital homomorphism from a unital C*-algebra into B(H) is similar to a *-homomorphism. The route is a universal bound ||[Y^(h),X]|| <= C g_P(Y)||X|| for every von Neumann algebra P, which reduces through Kirchberg's derivation criterion. A corollary gives one universal hyperreflexivity constant.

issues.description: The whole constant chain (c_row, c_0, c_1, C) rests on the row estimate ||phi||_row <= sqrt2 ||phi||^2 for bounded unital homomorphisms, quoted from Dickson 2014, Lemma 2.9, Eq. (19). I could not check that citation from the sources here. The step that derives the column bound from it via phi^sharp is correct.
issues.evidence: Cited only; the triangular-homomorphism reduction (norm of Phi <= 2, giving c_row = 4 sqrt2) checks out.

issues.description: A free increasing-matrix subfactor D inside Q^omega comes from Popa 2014, Theorem 0.1(a), applied twice with constant sequences. The hypotheses are verified (Q not intertwinable into C, and (Q^omega)' ∩ P^omega = C). The exact form of the cited moment-vanishing conclusion is taken on trust.
issues.evidence: The proof's restatement of Popa's theorem matches the known free-independence result for irreducible inclusions (Popa 1995/2014).

coverage:
Read every section in full (introduction, preliminaries, tensors, propagation, hankel, finite-factors, global). Steps checked line by line:
- Triangular-homomorphism and Paulsen metric computation (V = -d D11^{-1} D12; block identities checked).
- Cyclic column factorization via standard form, and the cyclic cb bound 4c_row.
- Symmetrization: hypothesis and compressed commutator are preserved.
- Invariant-intertwiner lemma: L^1 endpoint bound, Schur–Weyl stability across matrix stages, matrix-unit argument removing long cycles (threshold c(π) < 1+(k+l)/2), orthonormal-pool argument removing same-side pairings.
- Word-structure lemma.
- Full-column lemma: cyclic eHr ≅ eHr', N-fold extension to a right multiplier R_b with b = rb.
- Propagation: right supports, isometric prefixing on the non-scalar part, vanishing of the scalar part.
- Compression identity ι*[G,L_h]ι = [J,T_h] + error terms.
- Free compression: E_C(ebe) = u²b and ||ebe|| <= 2√u||b||_2 + u||b||.
- Hankel entries u(γ_{j−k} + γ_{j+k+1}s), with normalization t^{-1}u²/2 = u. Fourier coefficients sin(lθ)/(πl), lower bound ||H_f|| >= 1/(2π²), and ||h|| <= 3u.
- Matrix-block reduction in the finite-factor proposition (outer/copy indices, τ(s) = 0), averaging over R, ultrapower lifting of corners, and identification of the compression on constant vectors.
- Global part: type II_1 (embedding into L²(M)^{⊕ℕ}), properly infinite (isometry-row identity verified), type I_n, central decomposition, removal of separability, finite-column assembly of derivations, and the hyperreflexivity corollary.
As an independent cross-check, I tested the Hankel mechanism by hand on the explicit operators G_T (T applied to the last A_0-letter), and it matches. Not checked: the external citations (Dickson, Popa, Kirchberg/Ozawa, Christensen's cb-distance formula).
